beats.text: Feature-based drafters are like archers firing in the dark; they lack the target's deep recurrent history, leading to constant, expensive misfires.
beats.visual_focus: An archer missing a target in a dark room.

beats.text: Enter ReaDy. It transforms Hybrid Linear Attention states into a live, queryable database for every single draft position.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I've definitely dealt with speculative decoding latency, so calling out the 'wall' it hits caught me immediately. I like that you didn't waste time with a 'Hey guys' intro. I got lost for a second on 'Hybrid Linear Attention states'—I know what linear attention is, but the 'Hybrid' part felt like a buzzword without a quick clarification on what it's actually mixing. Otherwise, the technical breakdown felt like something I'd actually send to my study group.

Before you deploy your next architecture, consider this: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until ReaDy proved: hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting.
